name: Binomial probability
formula: P(\text{exactly } k \text{ successes in } n \text{ trials}) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}
whenToUse: A fixed number of independent trials, each with the same success probability, and the question asks for an exact number of successes.
example: A biased coin shows heads with probability $\frac{1}{3}$. Exactly $2$ heads in $5$ flips has probability $\binom{5}{2}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^3 = 10 \cdot \frac{1}{9} \cdot \frac{8}{27} = \frac{80}{243}$.
pitfall: Do not forget the factor $\binom{n}{k}$ for WHICH trials succeed. Without it you get the probability of one specific order.
